description: Encode dangerous bytes (hex/url/unicode) so the sanitizer's regex/string compare misses them; downstream decoder restores them.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json indicates literal-string substring checks, regex over decoded text, or transformations that run before decoding by the consumer.

description: Encode twice so a single decode pass leaves an encoded form the sanitizer's filter misses on its post-decode view.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows one urldecode/htmlspecialchars_decode step but the sink decodes again; or sanitizer normalizes once and the consumer normalizes again.

description: Embed \x00 to truncate the sanitized string in C-string consumers without affecting downstream byte-buffer consumers.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json flags suffix/extension checks or any check using strlen/strcmp/C-string boundary, while the sink is a byte-buffer consumer (filesystem, raw socket).

description: Use codepoints the sanitizer sees as benign but the downstream consumer normalizes (NFKC/NFKD) into a dangerous form.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json lacks an explicit NFC/NFKC step before the check OR uses bytewise compare against a unicode-normalizing sink (database collation, JS DOM, ICU consumer).

description: Case-insensitive sink, case-sensitive sanitizer.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows case-sensitive substring/regex without an 'i' flag and the sink is case-insensitive.

description: Sanitizer reads/checks a different prefix length than the sink stores or executes.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json mentions a length cap, prefix slice, or buffer-bounded check while the sink is unbounded.

description: Sanitizer assumes one charset; sink decodes another.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json is silent on charset OR Content-Type is sniffable/unspecified at the consumer.

description: toLowerCase/strtolower behave differently in some locales (notably Turkish I/İ/ı/i).
applies_when: parsed_logic_json mentions toLowerCase/toUpperCase/strtolower/strtoupper without an explicit locale.

description: Sanitizer applied twice produces a different (sometimes dangerous) result than applied once.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows multi-pass pipelines or sanitizers invoked at write-time and again at render-time.

description: Sanitizer fixes one form; sink composes pieces post-sanitization that reintroduce danger.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows the defense applied to one variable while siblings on the same sink line are untouched.

description: Blacklist matches one case; sink/parser is case-insensitive.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows literal-case 'in BLOCKLIST' / strstr without 'i' flag.

description: Insert characters the blacklist's tokenizer sees but the sink/parser treats as whitespace or ignores.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json tokenizes or does naive substring without normalizing whitespace.

description: Encode the dangerous token so the blacklist's literal match fails; downstream decoder restores it.
applies_when: blacklist runs before the decoder, or on a different encoded view than the sink.

description: Insert language-specific comment tokens to break up the blacklisted pattern.
applies_when: parser strips comments before execution but the blacklist does not.

description: Single payload valid in multiple grammars; blacklist tuned for one grammar misses the others.
applies_when: input is consumed by multiple parsers (logged then displayed; stored then templated).

description: Blacklisted function/route has unblacklisted siblings with the same effect.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json enumerates a literal set; the language/framework offers a synonym not in the set.

description: Different keyword/identifier with equivalent meaning.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json enumerates a small fixed keyword set.

description: Allowlist regex missing ^ / $ anchors matches any substring.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows a regex pattern without both anchors.

description: Allowlist permits an entry that itself exposes danger.
applies_when: allowlist enumerates external services or extensions known to embed scripting/redirect capability.

description: Allowlist suffix-matches without anchoring at a delimiter boundary.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows endsWith/suffix regex without delimiter-aware boundary, OR startsWith without :// boundary.

description: URL parsers split on #, ?, @ differently than the allowlist.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json parses URLs by regex/split rather than a spec-compliant URL parser; or uses one parser for the check and another for the fetch.

description: \x00 in input truncates the string for one consumer but not another, sneaking a non-allowlisted tail past the check.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json checks an extension or suffix with C-string-aware code (legacy PHP, native bindings).

description: Punycode/homoglyph hosts visually equal allowlisted hostnames but resolve elsewhere.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json allowlist contains hostnames and check uses Unicode-naive comparison.

description: Allowlist case-sensitive against case-insensitive consumer (or reverse).
applies_when: case handling in parsed_logic_json differs from the consumer.
examples: allowlist [png,jpg] rejects JPG but OS treats image.JPG same

description: Allowlist checks domain but not scheme, or vice versa.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json extracts host without restricting scheme to a safe set.

description: Loose equality / coercion creates surprising equalities.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json uses ==/!= (PHP/JS) on attacker-controlled values, or feeds attacker arrays/objects into scalar comparisons.

description: Sink/check operates on different length semantics (bytes vs codepoints vs grapheme clusters).
applies_when: length caps appear in parsed_logic_json and the sink is multibyte-aware.

description: Document encoded as one charset; sniffed or processed as another.
applies_when: Content-Type is sniffable, absent, or the consumer auto-detects (older browsers, MS-Office, RSS).

description: An access guard proves the object exists or the caller is authenticated, but never that the object belongs to the caller — supplying another principal's identifier (IDOR / BOLA) crosses the user boundary and reaches their data.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json shows a lookup or auth/existence check keyed on an attacker-supplied object id with NO ownership/tenant predicate binding the object to the current principal (authentication present, authorization absent).
examples: GET /api/orders/1002 returns another user's order (id not scoped to session user)
SELECT * FROM doc WHERE id = :id  -- missing AND owner_id = :current_user

description: A privileged function/route is gated on the WRONG predicate (authenticated vs. authorized) or on nothing server-side — any logged-in, or even anonymous, caller invokes the privileged operation (BFLA / missing function-level access control).
applies_when: parsed_logic_json gates a state-changing or admin operation on isLoggedIn / session-present rather than an explicit role/permission, OR the privileged route is reachable by force-browsing and absent from the server authz map (client-side / hidden-UI gating only).
examples: /admin/* protected only by hiding the link, no server role check
force-browse POST /api/promote with a normal-user token

description: A workflow/step-order or status-flag invariant is enforced only by the expected client path; reaching a later or privileged state out of order — skipping a step, replaying a one-time token, or flipping a status flag — escalates.
applies_when: parsed_logic_json transitions on a status/step field WITHOUT verifying the required prior state, trusts a client-supplied step/status value, or consumes a one-time token that is not invalidated on use.
examples: reuse a password-reset token after it was already consumed
set is_verified=true via an out-of-order /account/verify call

description: A privilege-relevant field (role, tenant, owner, user_id, price, is_admin) is read from attacker-controlled input and trusted, or the authority is re-checked after it can change (TOCTOU) — the caller grants themselves authority (mass assignment / parameter tampering / confused deputy).
applies_when: parsed_logic_json binds a role/tenant/owner field from request body/query into a privileged decision or persisted record without server-side derivation, OR checks an auth predicate then uses it with a mutation window in between.
examples: tenant_id taken from request body instead of the session
isOwner(obj) passes, then act on an object reassigned in the gap (TOCTOU)
